Forgetting is rarely an excuse for Her Highness-

Gods above…
Not even servants are to be present in the party.
Or have you forgotten?
It doesn’t matter.
What you need to right now is leave before Her Highness arrives-

Before Lady Amelia could finish her sentence, the grand doors of the Hall opened with a loud creak.
The herald’s voice echoed through the vast room.

Hear ye!
All rise for the arrival of The Jewel of Aurelium!
Her Royal Majesty, Princess Hailey!
Shoot.

Her Highness really is here…
By the look on Lady Amelia’s face, she really is unhappy that I’m still here.
Oh no.
Will I get punished for this?
How do you respond?

choices.text: I can still leave…
Try and sneak off
Freeze in terror

nodes.dialogueText: You probably should…
I presume you’re not too busy, Amelia?
Oh, am I interrupting something?
What’s the matter, dear? You look pale as a ghost.

Oh.
Uh…
Wow, She’s…
I can’t believe the Princess of Aurelium is right before me!
The murals portray her semblance poorly.
The air and aura she carries around her is very poised and elegant, it’s intimidating me.

Amelia, is our friend all right?
Perhaps they’re overworked…

E-Everything is fine, milady.
This servant was just finalizing the remaining arrangements before retiring for the night.
I see. See to it that they rest afterward. No one in my court should suffer in silence.
Hailey glances over her shoulder as heavy footsteps echo from the main entrance.
It seems our remaining guests have arrived.

I quickly step back toward the shadow of the pillars, trying to make myself as invisible as possible while keeping my head bowed.
Entering right behind Her Highness is a tall, handsome man with an effortlessly charming smile, accompanied by a sharp-eyed noble holding a ledger.

Prince Owen, Her Highness’s betrothed from the neighboring realm, alongside his secretary and cousin, Lord Robert.
While Prince Owen radiates a warm, regal authority, Lord Robert scans the hall with cool, calculating eyes—measuring every guard, exit, and noble in the room.
My fair Princess. You look radiant tonight, despite the sudden urgency of this gathering.
Your Highness. We have arrived as requested, though I trust this meeting will yield the diplomatic clarity our realm requires.
Welcome, Prince Owen, Lord Robert.

Standing directly at the threshold of the dais is a towering knight in polished silver plate, his hand never straying far from the pommel of his broadsword.
Sir Davor.

The Princess’s childhood friend and legendary shield. He guards her not merely as a knight guards his sovereign, but with a fierce, suffocating possessiveness—his hazel eyes glaring at anyone who dares step too close to Her Highness.
Your Highness, the hall is secure. Though... I still question the presence of foreign mages within your sanctuary.

Sir Davor’s gaze shifts toward the shadows behind Prince Owen, where a tall, cloak-wrapped figure glides silently into the room.
The Mage Emrys.
Prince Owen’s private bodyguard and a practitioner of forbidden arcane arts.
In a kingdom where magic is strictly outlawed, Emrys’s presence alone sends a chilling pressure through the air.
They say nothing, their glowing eyes fixed entirely on the silver goblet sitting atop the lectern.
Emrys is here under my personal protection, Sir Davor. There is no cause for alarm.
Peace, Davor. Tonight is a night for absolute truth, not petty squabbles.

Princess Hailey walks gracefully up the steps of the dais, her long dress rustling against the marble floor. Lady Amelia quickly steps forward to offer her the ceremonial silver goblet filled with blue spiced wine.
Your Goblet, Her Highness...
Thank you, Amelia.
Other guests are arriving. I should welcome them.

(I make my way down the carpeted hallway toward the Solarium Hall entrance. The low murmur of chatter begins to drift from the foyer as the remaining dignitaries step through the heavy brass doors.)
Other guests are arriving. I should welcome them.

As I approach the threshold, a hulking figure clad in a polished silver plate catches my eye. A heavy broadsword sits strapped to his waist, his hand resting on the pommel with practiced ease.
Sir Davor.
The Princess’s childhood companion and now her personal royal shield.
Tales of his martial prowess on the eastern front are legendary, but around the palace, he is known for a singular, unyielding obsession: the absolute safety of Her Highness.
He guards her not just like a knight guards a sovereign, but like a holy relic that must never be touched by common hands.
Hold your step, servant.
I freeze in place. His sharp, hazel eyes scan my uniform with intense suspicion before settling on my face.
Her Highness's personal dais is off-limits to secondary staff tonight. State your business in the hall.
How do you respond?

choices.text: I am making sure the entry is clear for the incoming delegates, Sir Davor.
I was just observing the guests, Sir.
Lower your head and step aside into a bow.

nodes.dialogueText: See that you do so swiftly. Keep your distance from the head table.
Observe from the perimeter. Do not let your gaze linger on the Princess.

…
Good. Know your place.
(Before Sir Davor can grill me further, the sound of smooth, cultured laughter echoes from the main courtyard doors.)
Now, now, Sir Davor. There is no need to terrify the household staff before the gathering has even officially commenced.
(Prince Owen and Lord Robert walk into frame)

Prince Owen.
The foreign prince betrothed to our Princess Hailey. He possesses a calm, almost hypnotic charisma that effortlessly commands the room.
Behind him follows Lord Robert, his secretary and cousin, carrying a leather-bound portfolio under his arm. While Prince Owen exudes warmth, Lord Robert’s sharp eyes measure every corner of the Solarium as if calculating its net worth.
We are guests in Princess Hailey’s pristine hall tonight. Let us accord her staff the grace she so effortlessly embodies.
My duty is her security, Prince Owen. Foreign delegations bring... unpredictability.
A prudent concern, Knight. Though I assure you, my Prince's intentions are entirely aligned with the Princess’s peace.
Lord Robert's gaze flickers past Sir Davor and falls squarely onto me.
You there. Servant.
How do you respond?

choices.text: How may I serve you, My Lord?
Welcome to the Solarium, Your Highness, My Lord.
Remain standing silently at attention.

nodes.dialogueText: Direct the courier carrying our realm's ceremonial gift to the private storage.
Thank you, young one. Your hospitality does your mistress credit.
Tsk. Lacks the crisp discipline of our northern court...
Peace, Robert. They are under enough stress tonight.

As the two foreign nobles move past, a cold draft sweeps through the corridor. A tall figure in dark, embroidered robes glides silently into the hall behind them, keeping to the deeper shadows along the wall.
The Mage Emrys.
Prince Owen’s private bodyguard and an infamous practitioner of the arcane.
In our kingdom, where magic is strictly forbidden and heavily persecuted, their presence here is a walking scandal. The sheer pressure radiating off their dark cloak makes my chest feel heavy.

Emrys doesn't speak to the staff, nor do they make eye contact. Their pale hand rests lightly against a hidden pocket in their robes as their glowing eyes fixedly monitor the dais where Princess Hailey's glass cup sits.
To think all these powerful, dangerous figures are gathered in one place...
It’s clear this is no simple celebration. Everyone carries a heavy weight on their shoulders tonight.
I bow deeply to the remaining guests as they take their positions across the Solarium Hall.
If I linger any longer, I risk drawing the ire of the nobles or Lady Amelia.
I should return to my station near the rear doors before Her Highness makes her grand entrance.
The air in the room feels heavy, almost suffocating. Every single person here—from the foreign prince to the reclusive mage—is watching every movement with bated breath.

Hear ye!
All rise for the arrival of The Jewel of Aurelium!
Her Royal Majesty, Princess Hailey!
The grand wooden doors swing wide open. As Princess Hailey steps into the hall, a collective hush falls over the room.

Oh.
Uh…
Wow. She’s…
I can’t believe the Princess of Aurelium is right before me!
The murals portray her semblance poorly. The air and aura she carries around her is overwhelmingly poised, elegant, and entirely commanding—yet beneath that surface, I can see the deep exhaustion etched around her eyes.

Amelia, is our staff all right?
The atmosphere feels... tense tonight.
E-Everything is under control, milady. Please, the court awaits your address.
Very well.

Princess Hailey glides gracefully up the marble steps of the dais. Lady Amelia steps forward, her hands trembling slightly as she hands Hailey the ceremonial silver goblet filled with the signature blue spiced wine.
Your goblet, Your Highness...
Thank you, Amelia.

Princess Hailey turns to face the gathered assembly.
Her gaze sweeps over Prince Owen, Lord Robert, Sir Davor, Lady Eris, and Emrys. For a split second, her eyes look tired—like someone who is finally putting down a burden she has carried for far too long.
My breath catches in my throat.
I am supposed to be a nobody here—a background servant who fades into the woodwork—but the sheer weight of what is happening pins me to the floor.
For years, you have built a pedestal beneath my feet... but tonight, I tear it down.
She raises the silver goblet to her lips and takes a deep, unhesitating drink.
Here's to more prosperity to the Kingdom. May you continue to put your faith in me, your divine Princess to service you forevermore.

Her Highness raises the silver goblet to her lips. She drinks. Once. Deeply. For a split second, the room hangs on her every breath—until her jaw locks.
Suddenly, her speech stutters. Her eyes widened in sharp, unfeigned shock.
The silver goblet slips from her fingertips, shattering against the marble floor with a deafening ring as dark blue veins instantly streak across her neck and jaw.

Ghk—!
What…?
Huh…?

The silver rings against the marble floor with a deafening chime, blue spiced wine splashing across the steps like spilled blood.
I watch in horror as dark, unnatural blue veins pulse violently beneath her pale skin, surging up her neck toward her jaw in jagged, creeping fractures.
YOUR HIGHNESS!!!
Hailey!

Before Owen or Davor can reach the dais, the heavy iron doors slam shut on their own with a thunderous crash. Runes of light flash across the stone walls as the castle’s automated Stasis Protocol locks the room down tight, sealing our fates to be trapped in this nightmarish room.
Sir Davor breaks first. His knightly composure vanishes into pure, unhinged instinct.
He doesn't just run—he lunges, his heavy boots cracking against the floor tiles as he hurls himself up the steps, his cloak flaring behind him like a wounded bird's wing.
Hailey! Look at me! Who did this to you?! Speak to me! Look at me!
Get back from her, Davor! Do not move her body!

The Prince drops to his knees beside her on the cold marble. His hands hover over her face—trembling violently.
The icy, controlled diplomat I saw moments ago is completely gone. His face is ghost-white, his jaw trembling with a raw, desperate terror that looks far too visceral, far too ugly to be performative.
She’s breathing, but her heart... It's erratic! It’s an alchemical paralytic!
N-No... No, no, no! I only poured what was in the official flask! I didn't—I swear by the Light, I didn't touch it!

Lady Amelia’s voice is sharp, borderline hysterical. She clutches at her white apron, hyperventilating so hard her shoulders heave as her wide, bloodshot eyes dart frantically between the shattered goblet and the Princess.
Is that the genuine panic of an innocent servant... or the frantic terror of someone whose calculated attempt just succeeded?
Gods above... Someone help her! Davor, do something! Owen!

Eris is crying, fat tears ruining her carefully applied cosmetics, but her gaze keeps flickering away from Hailey—toward the hearth, toward the private study door.
She looks smaller, stripped of her haughty noble air, but there is a strange, calculating panic in the way she clutches her lace handkerchief against her lips.
Everyone, remain where you are! Owen, step away from the dais—if this is a volatile foreign alchemical agent, touching her bare skin could contaminate you as well!

Lord Robert’s reaction chills me to the bone. He isn't crying. He isn't screaming.
He is already analyzing the room, his sharp eyes scanning the exits, the staff, the shattered glass, and the royal guests like a grandmaster assessing a ruined chessboard.

They don't even rush forward. They don't panic. Their glowing, inhuman eyes remain fixed entirely on the shattered glass and the pool of blue liquid, their pale hands twitching beneath their heavy robes as if channeling or suppressing a forbidden spell.
In a room bursting with noise and grief, their total silence feels like a quiet confession.
I take a shuddering step forward. My throat is dry as dust. Every instinct in my body tells me to run, to hide, to pretend I was never here, but before anyone can make a move toward the grand exit—
THOOM.

A deafening crash echoes through the hall, shaking the dust from the chandeliers. Heavy, enchanted stone slabs slam down over the main doors and windows with absolute finality, sealing out the night.
Golden wards flare along the walls, burning bright before settling into a sickening, rhythmic pulse.
The Royal Stasis Protocol. The castle’s automated anti-treason ward has triggered. We are locked in.
The doors! Who locked the doors?!
It’s the automated Stasis Ward. A silent distress signal has already been broadcast to the High Inquisitor's Garrison outside... Look at the way the room lit up.
What... what does the cadence mean?! Robert, speak!
It means in exactly twenty minutes... the outer barrier will shatter, and the execution squad will breach this room.
The Royal Families’ knights have been notified that something happened in this room.
For a kingdom that forbids magic, they sure have impressive arcane security measures.
Twenty minutes?! We’ll be slaughtered! They don't take prisoners when a royal is poisoned! They'll purge the entire hall!
Twenty minutes.
My mind races violently against the thumping of my own heart.

The Inquisitors won't care who is a humble servant and who is a foreign prince—if Princess Hailey dies and no proven culprit or antidote is produced when those doors shatter, everyone in this room will be put to the sword to cleanse the treason.
I look at Princess Hailey. Her eyes peacefully closed. She is completely paralyzed, her chest barely rising, unable to speak a single word or move a single finger.

I can't just stand here and wait to be executed. I know this hall.
I know where the wine was poured, who walked where, and what was hidden in her private study.
If no one else is going to look at this logically because of their panic or their guilt... I have to.
We need to move her off this cold floor! The private study—there’s a sofa inside!
You step into her private quarters over my dead body, foreigner! You brought that cursed wine!

Feeling the precious seconds ticking away , something inside me snaps.
I step directly between the armed knight and the desperate prince, forcing my voice not to shake.
Sir Davor! Standing here arguing will kill her faster than the poison! Help His Highness carry her to the study sofa, or her blood is on your hands!

...You dare speak to me—ghk!
Fine!
But I am holding the threshold! No one touches her without my eyes on them!

Owen nods at me—a brief, sharp look of genuine gratitude breaking through his panic—before carefully carrying Princess Hailey into the private study. The rest of the nobles filter inside behind him, the atmosphere thick enough to choke on.

Twenty minutes. The blue veins on her neck are already darkening to a bruised purple.
I have less than a third of an hour to find the antidote and name the killer... or we all die in this room.

I follow the panicked crowd into the Private Study as Owen gently places Princess Hailey onto the velvet sofa.
The heavy oak door behind us remains half-ajar, guarded rigidly by Davor. The air inside the study is suffocating, smelling of old parchment, cold hearth ash, and the metallic tang of fear.

I inspect the corner near the entrance pillars where Prince Owen, Lord Robert, and Emrys stood before the speech commenced.
